_readme.what: The frozen catalogue. lib/checkout/listings.ts reads this and NOTHING ELSE — no listing is fetched while a demo is running.
_readme.shape: { _readme, listings: Listing[] } where Listing is lib/checkout/types.ts's Listing, exactly: listingId, retailer, title, productUrl, imageUrl, priceMinor, currency, dimensionsMm.
_readme.units: priceMinor is an INTEGER OF CENTS. dimensionsMm is millimetres, or null.
_readme.provenance: listingId, title, productUrl, imageUrl and priceMinor were fetched live from IKEA's own search backend (sik.search.blue.cdtapps.com) on 2026-09-19, and every productUrl was checked to return a page whose rel=canonical is a /p/ product page.
_readme.dimensions: dimensionsMm is filled ONLY where IKEA's own measure string gives an unambiguous width x depth x height. Everywhere else it is null, which renders as 'no dimensions listed' and a muted fit badge. Estimating a carton here would feed lib/fit.ts a number nobody measured, and the fit verdict is the one rigorous thing in the product.
_readme.retailers: Every row is IKEA. Amazon, Target, Wayfair, West Elm, CB2 and Etsy all block automated reads (403/429), so no product URL at those shops could be verified, and an unverified URL that quietly redirects to a category page is worse on stage than none.
_readme.replacing: Tian's scraper overwrites this file. Keep the shape and the units; add rows for the other retailers and fill dimensionsMm from the listing's own quoted measurements.
